links.outcome: Whether patients recognize potentially harmful chatbot health advice
links.effect: Specialists rated usefulness (3.93 vs 4.59) and correctness (4.62 vs 3.84) significantly lower for potentially harmful ChatGPT responses (P<.001); patients did not.
links.quote: Alarmingly, patients are not able to independently recognize these potential dangers.

links.outcome: Whether users detect incorrect or harmful AI outputs
links.effect: Specialists rated potentially harmful ChatGPT responses lower on usefulness (3.93 vs 4.59) and correctness (4.62 vs 3.84), P<.001; patients showed no such difference.
links.quote: Alarmingly, patients are not able to independently recognize these potential dangers.

screen.reason: Empirical study evaluating ChatGPT responses versus expert physician responses on clinical questions, rated by both patients and physicians in a blinded offline study. It evaluates model performance and patient perception rather than a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
